newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end higher on late bargain hunting.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end higher on late bargain hunting.

text.p: Late bargain hunting droved Thai stocks to close higher after they stayed in the negative territory all day on lingering concern about weak economic indicators, brokers said on Friday.
The SET index turned bullish 10 minutes before closing, advancing 9.23 points to 835.71 on thin 2.2 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index rose 0.77 point to 62.06.
"Late bargain hunting by local investors combined with buying by companies seeking to dress up year-end balance sheets helped push the index up," said Virat Tippanontakul of First Asia Securities.
The central bank said the October current account deficit narrowed to 30.2 billion baht from 30.5 billion in September but trade deficit widened to 36.2 billion baht from 25 billion.
Bangkok Bank topped the active list, falling one baht to 193, Securities One gained six to 119, TelecomAsia surged one to 54, Siam Cement lost 20 to 772, and Loxley rose three to 175.
Brokers see support for the index at 800 and its resistance at 840 on Monday.
